title: FamilySearch Full-Text Search and Transkribus make handwritten records searchable with AI; no specific discovery documented
summary: FamilySearch introduced AI handwriting-recognition full-text search via FamilySearch Labs in 2024; Transkribus (READ-COOP) reports 200+ million pages deciphered. Makers' accounts only; no finding.
account: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints newsroom (2 January 2025), reviewing FamilySearch's 2024, states that FamilySearch 'can convert an image of text into a machine-readable text format, allowing users to search the full text of the records' using handwriting recognition and OCR, that Full-Text Search was introduced through FamilySearch Labs in 2024, and that 2.5 billion searchable records and images were added overall; it gives no example of a user discovery. Transkribus, developed by the European cooperative READ-COOP SCE, says on its site that it 'turns centuries of handwriting into text you can search, study, and share', claims more than 500,000 users and 200 million pages deciphered, and cites projects such as the University of Georgia transcribing 20,000 pages in two months and Archion's portal of more than 200,000 German church books. The earlier verifier found no independent source documenting a specific discovery, reunion or entitlement from either system; FamilySearch's help article on full-text search returned HTTP 403 here. The date is the newsroom article date; the feature launched in 2024.
purpose: Make handwritten historical records searchable by converting images to text with AI handwriting recognition
system: FamilySearch Full-Text Search (handwriting recognition and OCR); Transkribus (READ-COOP SCE)
deployer: FamilySearch Labs; archives and research projects using Transkribus (University of Georgia, Archion)
location: Global (FamilySearch users; European and US archives)
taxonomy_note: Only the makers' accounts (the FamilySearch parent organization's newsroom and the Transkribus website) could be fetched, and neither names a specific discovery; general benefit with all depths null. Two systems are named because the earlier reason examined both; FamilySearch is listed first as the focus of that search.

ratings.reason: No documented individual discovery or reunion.

ai_role.statement: Handwriting-recognition models produce the searchable text in both systems; the only sources fetched are the makers' own (the Church newsroom for FamilySearch, the Transkribus site), which give capability and volume claims but no specific verified finding.
